history.dynasty: Portuguese colonial period (temple destroyed 1567); present structure 18th century
history.summary: CSV town is WRONG: this temple is at Bandora (Bandivade), Ponda taluka, North Goa - not Vasco da Gama. Originated around the 15th century; Portuguese records list the Mahalaxmi (Malcumi) temple among those destroyed in 1567. During the Portuguese Inquisition era, two devotees (Safto and Fato) smuggled the idol out of Colva in a trunk at night, first to Talauli near Ponda (where the goddess's footprints are still worshipped), then to Bandora, where it was installed alongside the existing idol - so the temple now houses two idols of Mahalaxmi. The deity wears a linga on her head (her satvika/peaceful form); the temple is the kuldevi of many Saraswat families. The current 18th-century structure has a silver arched doorway, 24 wooden panels depicting Bhagavata Purana scenes, a monolithic medieval deepastamba, and a sabhamandapa art gallery with 22 woodcarvings of the Vyuha - considered rare in the subcontinent.

name: Shree Mahalaxmi Temple
town_description: Bandora (also Bandivade) is a village in Ponda taluka, North Goa, about 4 km from Ponda town and 28 km from Panaji. It is known as a Goan temple town, housing several major Hindu temples including Mahalaxmi and the Shantadurga temple at nearby Kavale.

travel.airport: Goa International Airport, Dabolim (~28 km) or Manohar International Airport, Mopa
travel.road: Well-connected by road; ~4 km from Ponda town, with local bus and taxi services from Panaji and Margao.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri and the annual zatra (March-April) for festive darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM to 8:30 PM daily; poojas 7:00-11:30 AM, 12:00 PM and 8:00 PM. Entry free.
